ops.title: capt-hook subagent denylist declines, never blocks
ops.body: Live-verified 2026-07-16 on yasyf-home (capt-hook 9.24.0, CC 2.1.211). Benign subagent tools get explicit permissions.py allow rows; destructive commands (rm -rf) are declined — no allow row — but a defaultMode:auto session runs the declined call natively with NO dialog. Mechanism pinned by disambiguation: CC auto-mode classifier, NOT the --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions flag (benign calls still needed capt-hook's allow, ruling out a blanket native skip) and NOT CC permission caching (rm-first fresh session reproduced it). So 'destructive still prompts' holds only in sessions whose permission mode would prompt on a declined call. Escalation path if a hard guarantee is ever wanted: an active deny() on the destructive patterns — deny() defaults to PreToolUse|PermissionRequest since 9.24.0 and deny-wins beats the approve.
